rationale: This is essentially the archived "Depreciation Conservatism Book Interaction" with RANK(B/M) swapped for SUMRANK(B/M, E/P), a cosmetic re-weighting of the value leg whose stated motivation (reducing value-factor exposure) is backwards since adding earnings yield increases, not reduces, HML loading.

A defensible, mechanism-driven refinement of the archive's strongest result — industry-adjusting the own-history depreciation surprise removes sector-common accounting/asset-mix variation and is a genuinely different conditioning construct rather than a rescaling, though it remains a close relative of that prior signal.

Near-duplicate of the archived "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap" (same scaled depreciation-shortfall conditioner, same sign, same construction) with only the value leg widened to SUMRANK, so it adds little new information beyond the already-evaluated short side.

A coherent and previously untested conditioner (D&A addback dependence of OCF as unpriced capital consumption) that complements rather than duplicates the archive's working-capital and maintenance-depreciation work, though dpc/(|oancf|+|ib|) is largely a capital-intensity/industry proxy so any result will need an industry-neutral robustness check.

The sign logic is internally consistent and the txach interpretation is correct, but this is substantially a sign-flipped repackaging of the archived "Tax Deferred Cash Yield Trap" (same conditioner, same scaler, adjacent value leg) whose positive fmb slope came with negligible alpha and ~6% coverage, so the "new" evidence is likely the same underlying result relabeled.

The acceleration framing is a legitimately distinct construct from the archive's level and one-period-change accrual conditioners, but taking a second difference of a ratio whose numerator is already an annual first difference stacks three layers of annual noise and will require several extra years of history, so expect weak power and degraded coverage.
